comment: Items are CONTENT, like materials.json and glyphs.json — not look-and-feel knobs like tuning.json. This file holds an item's BEHAVIOUR: its id, the kind the engine switches on, and its damage numbers. THE ART IS NOT HERE, and it is not part of any creature either: each item owns <id>.vox plus an <id>.json sidecar carrying its grip and its cutting edge. A held item BORROWS a rig slot, so while worn it is a real rig part — severable with the arm, droppable as debris, carvable per voxel — but its geometry has its own origin, so a weapon can never inflate the box of the body holding it. That was a real bug: as a rig prop the sword reached 30 micro outside mina's prefab box and drew her body offset from her own arm. Hot-reloads on R alongside materials and glyphs.
kinds: melee = swung, and cuts along the `edge` segment its own sidecar declares (see scripts/gen_sword_item.py). The blade geometry is what decides the wound; `carveBonus` only widens it.

items.desc: A straight double-edged arming sword. Held point-up; it cuts with the length of its blade, so where you land it is where the wound opens.
